text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Guntis Ulmanis nominated Andris Shkele to form a new government. Shkele said not all the factions of the old government will be allowed in the new one with the most to be excluded the Unity Party.
- The Swedish government announced that it was ready to cancel visa regulations for Latvians by this summer on condition that the Baltic states sign the 1949 Geneva Convention on Refugees.

- Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves paid a one-day official visit to Latvia. Birkavs and Ilves exchanged ratification letters for the agreement on social guarantees for residents of both countries.
- The heads of working parties for military cooperation between Latvia and the U.S. said defence co-operation between has developed successfully.
- New Russian ambassador Alexander Udaltsov received confirmation from the Russian State Duma that it has invited Latvian speaker Alfred Chepanis to visit the Russian Parliament on February 17-18.
- U.S. Congress member Gerald Solomon submitted to Congress a draft resolution which calls for the earliest possible integration of the Baltic States into NATO.
- Latvia's Way faction leader Andrejs Panteleyevs said the new cabinet would be based on a coalition treaty which is to be signed before the new government is put to the vote.
- President Guntis Ulmanis will visit Turkey February 18-21. The programme of the visit includes meetings with Turkish officials and signing of several international agreements.
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs leaves for Davos to participate in the World's Economic Forum.
- The newspaper gave an unofficial model of the new government which includes Democratic Party leader Ziedonis Chevers as interior minister and non-party specialist Janis Platais as finance minister.
- Residents of a nine-storey apartment bloc were evacuated after a discovered a stock German weapons and ammunition, dating from World War Two in the cellar.

- Despite election law restrictions, which bans him from running in the municipal election, the mayor of major eastern town Daugavpils has decided to join the list of Latvia's Social Democratic Labour party, the third most popular party in Latvia according to opinion polls.
